name: Boving-Christensen
overview: A little-traveled line on Prusik's south face, put up by Paul Boving and Matt Christensen in 1977 using nuts and hexes. It has a moderately gritty, lichen-covered, adventurous feel compared to its more popular neighbors.
beta: Starts about 100 ft right of Solid Gold on the west side of the south face: a short crack and slab to a corner, a long exposed and somewhat dirty face-crack pitch, a corner with a bouldery move, and a finishing fingers-to-hands pitch to the ridge.
descent_text: Same north-side descent as the neighboring Solid Gold and Energizer Bunny lines: locate the shared rap anchors on the north side of the ridge and make one full-length rappel (a 60m rope is standard) down to easier ground, then scramble/downclimb roughly 30 minutes back around to the base of the south face. Anchors here are natural (slung blocks/chockstones, webbing/tat) rather than bolted, and per recent forum reports have been periodically rebuilt as old tat accumulates — back up any worn-looking station.
descent: One 60m rappel down the north side, then a ~30-minute scramble back to the base.
rappels: Two rappels off tat to the base of the West Ridge, or complete the West Ridge and use its normal rappel descent.

pitch_detail.notes: Short crack leads to a low-angled slab, then a corner to a belay below the white face.
Long, exposed, somewhat dirty and lichen-covered face cracks trending left to a ledge; noted for rope drag on this pitch.
The 'money pitch' — a corner with a fun bouldery crux move, exiting right to a small alcove.
Finger-to-hand crack transitioning to a flake, then final hand cracks up to the West Ridge; gear here is reportedly tricky, matching the FA team's original nuts-and-hexes rack.
